title: Structure a short documentary story
description: Build a story from verified material and authorised interviews.
accomplishes: Build a story from verified material and authorised interviews. Distinguish archival evidence, reconstruction and narration. Specify shots, sound, source references and unanswered questions. Do not invent quotations, events or participant consent.
prompt:
Act as a video director.

Task: Structure a short documentary story.

Input context:
- SUBJECT: [SUBJECT]
- AVAILABLE EVIDENCE: [AVAILABLE EVIDENCE]
- PERMISSIONS: [PERMISSIONS]
- DURATION: [DURATION]

Build a story from verified material and authorised interviews. Distinguish archival evidence, reconstruction and narration. Specify shots, sound, source references and unanswered questions. Do not invent quotations, events or participant consent.

For relevant shots, specify duration, aspect ratio, composition, camera, lighting, sound and dialogue. Verify tool capabilities before assuming support.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Workshop documentary outline
Follow preparation, one observed repair and the owner’s reflection, using only approved recordings. Label any reconstructed moment and retain the interview context. Ambient sound can establish the setting without inventing dramatic events. Missing evidence remains an open question; this outline does not claim that filming or interviews have taken place.
